Why policy dates and project status matter

Renewable-energy policies establish objectives and incentives, while installed-capacity statistics describe development already recorded. Competitive-exam questions may present policy targets as though they are achieved figures. These categories must be kept separate.

The following milestones describe major developments relevant to Gujarat and India, using information available up to 16 November 2026.

National and Gujarat milestones

Date or periodDevelopmentStatus or significance
9 October 2022Modhera declared India's first 24x7 solar-powered villageSolar generation and battery-storage demonstration
4 January 2023National Green Hydrogen Mission approvedNational programme for hydrogen production, use and exports

29 February 2024PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana approvedResidential rooftop-solar programme

10 October 20253 major ports recognised as Green Hydrogen HubsIncludes Deendayal Port, Gujarat

30 September 2026MNRE Gujarat renewable-capacity snapshot55,511.46 MW installed renewable capacity

National Green Hydrogen Mission

The Union Cabinet approved the National Green Hydrogen Mission on 4 January 2023, with an initial financial outlay of ₹19,744 crore. It aims to promote domestic green-hydrogen production, reduce dependence on fossil-based inputs in suitable sectors, build industrial capabilities and develop export opportunities.

The mission envisages at least 5 million metric tonnes of green-hydrogen production capacity per year by 2030, associated with approximately 125 GW of additional renewable-energy capacity. These are programme objectives, not claims that those quantities had already been achieved at the November 2026 content cutoff.

Gujarat Integrated Renewable Energy Policy 2025

The Gujarat Integrated Renewable Energy Policy 2025 was issued on 24 December 2025. The policy aims to expand renewable electricity while addressing grid connectivity, storage, rooftop generation and other implementation issues.

Its broad capacity objectives include:

  • More than 100 GW of renewable capacity by 2030.
  • More than 150 GW of installed renewable capacity by 2035.
  • 300 GW of installed renewable capacity by 2047.

The policy also promotes battery energy storage, transmission strengthening, wind repowering, distributed solar installations, appropriate rooftop-metering arrangements and recycling of renewable-energy equipment.

The 2025 integrated policy superseded the earlier Gujarat Renewable Energy Policy 2023, while providing transitional provisions for eligible projects previously sanctioned. For current-policy questions, the 2023 policy should not be treated as the latest integrated policy.

Gujarat Green Hydrogen Policy 2025

Gujarat separately issued the Gujarat Green Hydrogen Policy 2025 in December 2025. Its mission is to develop production, consumption and export of green hydrogen and its derivatives.

The policy sets a target of 3 million metric tonnes per annum of green-hydrogen production capacity by 2035. Its stated objectives include approximately 30 GW of electrolyser capacity and 75 GW of renewable-energy capacity associated with the broader green-hydrogen ambition.

The policy text provides for operation until 31 December 2035 or the announcement of a replacement policy, whichever occurs earlier, with commencement tied to notification in the State's Official Gazette. These are policy provisions and targets, not verified installed production figures.

Different targets have different meanings

India's target of at least 5 million metric tonnes per year of green hydrogen by 2030 belongs to the National Green Hydrogen Mission. Gujarat's target of 3 million metric tonnes per year of green-hydrogen production capacity by 2035 belongs to the state's Green Hydrogen Policy 2025. Gujarat's renewable-electricity capacity targets belong to its Integrated Renewable Energy Policy 2025. These figures must not be interchanged.

Distinguishing development stages

TermWhat it meansWhat it does not prove
Resource potentialEstimated energy that might be technically availableThat generating facilities exist
Policy targetQuantity intended for a future dateThat the target has been achieved
Project announcedA proposed development has been publicly describedThat construction is complete
Project commissionedThe facility has entered service after required commissioningThat it always operates at full rated output
Electricity generatedActual electrical energy produced during a stated periodThat the same numerical value is installed capacity

Putting the complete subtopic together

Gujarat's solar and wind geography provides the natural resource base. Solar parks, rooftop systems and wind farms convert those resources into electricity. Transmission networks deliver electricity to consumers, while storage helps manage variations in supply.

Green hydrogen adds another use for renewable electricity. It allows suitable industries to substitute low-emission hydrogen for fossil-derived hydrogen and creates opportunities for producing green ammonia. Gujarat's refineries, fertilizer and chemical industries provide possible customers, while Kandla and other ports provide transport and potential export connections.

Each part of this development chain has limitations. Renewable electricity varies with weather; hydrogen production requires purified water and additional energy conversion; and projects must address land use, biodiversity, costs and infrastructure. The strongest understanding of Gujarat's energy transition is therefore both geographical and industrial, rather than merely a list of project names.

Prelims focus

  • National Green Hydrogen Mission: approved on 4 January 2023; initial outlay ₹19,744 crore.
  • National green-hydrogen objective: at least 5 million metric tonnes per year by 2030.
  • Gujarat Integrated Renewable Energy Policy 2025: more than 100 GW renewable capacity by 2030.
  • Gujarat Green Hydrogen Policy 2025: 3 million metric tonnes per year of green-hydrogen production capacity by 2035.
  • Deendayal Port was recognised as a Green Hydrogen Hub in October 2025.
  • Trap: A target, an estimate, a land allotment, an operating facility and actual annual generation describe different stages or measurements.

[Sources: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Cabinet Approval of the National Green Hydrogen Mission, 4 January 2023; Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Green Hydrogen Standard for India, Office Memorandum dated 18 August 2023; Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Policy and Regulatory Updates, December 2025, Gujarat Integrated Renewable Energy Policy 2025 and Gujarat Green Hydrogen Policy 2025 sections, printed pp. 10-12; Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, State-wise Location-based Installed Capacity of Renewable Power as on 30 September 2026, Gujarat row; Press Information Bureau, Three Major Ports Recognised as Green Hydrogen Hubs, 10 October 2025; Press Information Bureau, Modhera Solar Village announcement, 9 October 2022; official sources consulted 16 November 2026.]
